Plot module-level rhythm remodeling in polar coordinates

Source: R/plot_module.R
plot_module_polar.Rd

This function draws a polar scatter plot for one rhythm-state module. Each gene is represented by two points, one for each compared group. The angular coordinate represents peak phase, the radial coordinate represents rhythmic amplitude, and line segments connect the same gene across the two groups.

Usage

plot_module_polar(
  gene_meta,
  module_id,
  group1,
  group2,
  q_cut = 0.05,
  amp_cut = 0.1,
  n_gene = 30,
  n_label = 8,
  pt_size = 3.2,
  label_size = 3.2,
  title = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  Verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

gene_meta

A data.frame returned by infer_rhythm_module(). It must contain "gene" and "module_map" columns, as well as group-specific rhythm parameter columns.

module_id

An integer or character value specifying the module to plot.

group1

A character vector specifying the first group. This should usually match group1 used in infer_rhythm_module().

group2

A character vector specifying the second group. This should usually match group2 used in infer_rhythm_module().

q_cut

A numeric value specifying the FDR cutoff used to define rhythmic genes. Defaults to 0.05.

amp_cut

A numeric value specifying the minimum amplitude required for selected genes. Defaults to 0.10.

n_gene

An integer specifying the number of top-ranked genes to plot. Defaults to 30.

n_label

An integer specifying the number of top-ranked genes to label. Defaults to 8.

pt_size

A numeric value specifying point size. Defaults to 3.2.

label_size

A numeric value specifying gene-label size. Defaults to 3.2.

title

A character value specifying the plot title. If NULL, the title is set to "M" followed by module_id. Defaults to NULL.

palette

A named list specifying optional palettes for module and group. If NULL, default module colors and default scRhythmBayes group colors are used. Defaults to NULL.

Verbose

Logical; if TRUE, progress messages are printed.

Value

Invisibly returns a list containing the processed plotting data, paired gene table, selected labels, top genes, parameter-column map, and a ggplot object.

Details

Genes are selected from a module result table returned by infer_rhythm_module(). The function automatically detects group-specific rhythm parameter columns such as "Phase_A", "Amplitude_A", and "FDR_A". The alternative column style "phi_A", "A_A", and "q_A" is also supported.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data("srb_example_data")

res_phase <- infer_cell_phase(
  count = srb_example_data$Count,
  metadata = srb_example_data$meta,
  ZT_by = "ZT",
  strata_by = "celltype",
  Species = "mouse",
  setseed = 1,
  Verbose = FALSE
)

cell_use <- as.character(srb_example_data$meta$celltype) == "1"

res_param <- infer_gene_param(
  count = srb_example_data$Count[, cell_use, drop = FALSE],
  metadata = srb_example_data$meta[cell_use, , drop = FALSE],
  theta_pred = res_phase$theta_pred[cell_use],
  r_cell = res_phase$r_cell[cell_use],
  strata_by = "condition",
  ZT_by = "ZT",
  B = 5,
  n_worker = 1,
  setseed = 1,
  Verbose = FALSE
)

res_module <- infer_rhythm_module(
  param_wide = res_param$param_wide,
  compare_by = "condition",
  group1 = "A",
  group2 = "B",
  out_dir = NULL,
  Verbose = FALSE
)

p_polar <- plot_module_polar(
  gene_meta = res_module$module_result,
  module_id = 7,
  group1 = "A",
  group2 = "B"
)

p_polar$plot
} # }
